target_customer: DevOps, IoT and application engineering teams that need to store and analyze time series data
problem: Metrics, events and sensor data needed a purpose-built database; open source options like Graphite and OpenTSDB were not being pushed forward, per the founders.
business_model: Open source core with commercial cloud and enterprise subscriptions

founders.name: Paul Dix
founders.background_notes: Creator of InfluxDB and author of Service Oriented Design with Ruby per the YC page. Evan Kaplan joined as CEO in 2016 and is not described as a founder.

competitors.name: New Relic
competitors.traction_then: Named by Errplane's launch post as a rival

competitors.name: Pingdom
competitors.traction_then: Named by Errplane's launch post as a rival

competitors.name: Airbrake
competitors.traction_then: Named by Errplane's launch post as a rival

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a distributed, high-ingest time series database from scratch is hard for a small team; the founders wrote their own after finding Graphite and OpenTSDB inadequate.

defensibility.rationale: Open source adoption with large installed base and data lock-in, though open source licensing lets others compete and cloud vendors offer alternatives.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Monitoring vendors stayed focused on SaaS monitoring while InfluxData sold the database; it has remained independent through five rounds.

market_need_then: In 2013 the founders found that Graphite and OpenTSDB were not advancing fast enough for growing demand to handle time series data, and Errplane customers exposed raw metrics needs.

branding.name_origin: Errplane was renamed to InfluxData in late 2015 so the company name followed its InfluxDB product.
branding.brand_signature: InfluxDB as the name of the time series database category

rebrands.why: The company dropped the monitoring application to sell the InfluxDB database underneath it.

branding.community_and_virality: Open source project with a large user base, 1.3 million active instances and billions of Telegraf downloads per the company about page.

brand_strength.rationale: InfluxDB became the best known open source time series database, with the company claiming it defined the category; the company name followed the product.

pivots.to: InfluxDB open source time series database
pivots.why: Founders decided after Monitorama in September 2013 to build the database underneath their product.

outcome_analysis: Errplane pivoted in late 2013 from SaaS monitoring to the open source InfluxDB, raised five rounds from 2014 to 2023 totaling about 171 million dollars in equity, and renamed to InfluxData in 2015. The open source adoption and rise of DevOps and IoT drove growth to over 2,600 enterprise customers, though it laid off about 27 percent of staff in November 2022.
notes: The YC listing is for the company that launched as Errplane in the Winter 2013 batch. Series A date conflict: December 2014 in most sources, one database says 9.1M on 2014-11-21 (outlier). Series E also came with a 30M Silicon Valley Bank debt facility, not recorded as a round. The 2022 layoff of about 65 people is from a layoff tracker and a forum, unverified. A search snippet names Todd Persen as a co-founder of Errplane; not recorded because I did not open a source stating it. Series D in 2019 has no separate stage code so series_d_plus is used.
